newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian race row party officially registered.
newsitem.headline: Australian race row party officially registered.

text.p: Australian race row politician Pauline Hanson's One Nation Party has won official approval as a political party, electoral authorities said on Wednesday.
The Australian Electoral Commission approved One Nation as a party last Friday after it met relatively simply criteria governing political registration, a commission official said.

Several community and ethnic groups had lodged official objections to One Nation's registration, attacking it as racist and divisive. "Because the application complied with the guidelines, it was approved," the official told Reuters.

Hanson's party, which opposes immigration, Aboriginal welfare and foreign investment, already claims several thousand members after a nationwide publicity blitz and has forged a strong showing in leading opinion polls.
The party's 10 percent support would be enough to oust the leftist Australian Democrats as the third political power if maintained to the next election, due by mid-1999.
Hanson is the party's only member of any parliament.
She won a seat in the national parliament's lower house as an independent in 1996 after being dumped by Prime Minister John Howard's Liberal Party over her controversial views.
But Hanson has vowed to field scores of candidates in the next election and could win an influential role in the upper house Senate, where the voting system favours smaller parties.
One Nation officials say up to 50,000 application forms have been requested, but does not say how many members it has.
Functions to launch the party around Australia have sparked sometimes violent anti-Hanson protests. Protestors generally heavily outnumber supporters.

Registration as a political party allows candidates to use the party name on ballot papers and qualifies the party to apply for public funding for election campaigns, the electoral commission official said.
